title: ChatDesign: Bootstrapping Generative Floor Plan Design With Pre-trained Large Language Models
task: 交互式平面图生成与编辑
inputData: 自然语言需求及多种用户交互（文本、语音、点击、拖拽），统一转换为标准化操作与几何参数
contribution: 提出ChatDesign，将预训练大语言模型用于自然语言驱动的平面图生成，并通过统一指令翻译器将不同交互形式映射为Locate、Move、Resize、Add和Delete等结构化操作，实现迭代生成与局部编辑。
abstract: Large language models have achieved remarkable success in language-centered tasks, but architectural floor plan generation requires satisfying complex spatial and relational constraints. ChatDesign leverages pre-trained LLMs to generate floor plans from natural-language descriptions and supports iterative modifications based on user interaction. The framework combines initial text-driven generation with repeated refinement, allowing users to adjust designs through standardized editing operations.
methodology: The workflow starts from a user's textual description to produce an initial floor plan through an LLM-based generation pipeline. A Uniform Instructions Translator normalizes text, audio, mouse-click, and drag-and-drop interactions into five explicit operations—Locate, Move, Resize, Add, and Delete—with object, location, and geometric parameters, so later turns can modify the existing plan in a consistent machine-operable form.
results: On the main comparison, ChatDesign achieved Micro/Macro IoU values of 58.31/55.43, outperforming Tell2Design at 54.34/53.30; the iterative ChatDesign variant reached 54.57/57.24, while human layouts scored 64.67/62.32. On ten challenging Tell2Design cases, ChatDesign achieved 56.82/60.56 versus 47.56/51.10, showing a roughly 9–10 point improvement in both metrics.
taskEn: Interactive floor plan generation and editing
inputDataEn: Natural-language requirements and multimodal user interactions (text, voice, clicks, and drag-and-drop), normalized into structured operations and geometric parameters
operationEvidence: ChatDesign generates floor-plan alternatives from user requirements and implements Locate, Move, Resize, Add, and Delete operations that modify an existing floor-plan state through structured operation parameters.
